definition: Family resemblance is an approach for describing a field by the overlapping links among its parts rather than by one single defining feature. In this context, it highlights how knowledge, practices, values, methods, institutions, and social setting connect to one another.

reasons: The packet does not define the Family Resemblance Approach as a method for describing a field by overlapping links rather than a single defining feature; that interpretive claim is unsupported.

The packet supports relationships among geographical knowledge, evidence, methods, values, institutions, and social context, but it does not support the broader generalized phrasing about how the approach works across a field.
The packet does not provide a definition of “family resemblance” as an approach based on “overlapping links among its parts rather than one single defining feature.”

While the packet mentions that the study is “Guided by the Family Resemblance Approach (FRA)” and discusses relationships among “knowledge, evidence, methods, values, institutions,” it does not support the specific characterization in the definition of family resemblance itself as a general descriptive method in that manner.

The definition’s phrasing that family resemblance “highlights how knowledge, practices, values, methods, institutions, and social setting connect to one another” is only partially mirrored by the packet’s focus on relationships among knowledge/evidence/methods/values/institutions, but the packet does not support the broader “social setting” component as part of the term’s definition.
